newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stevedores reject strike talk condition.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stevedores reject strike talk condition.

text.p: Brazilian stevedores have rejected part of a proposal laying the foundation for fresh talks with steel firm Cosipa to resolve a labor dispute at the root of a strike at Santos, an official said.

Stevedores at Santos port began an indefinite strike at 0700 local/1000 GMT Tuesday over a decision by Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) to use its own workers to load and unload vessels at its private terminal.
In preliminary talks on Tuesday, the company laid out four basic points as a pre-condition to restarting official negotiations, a spokeswoman for Cosipa said.

Union delegates today voted on the proposal, approving three out of the four points. They have agreed to the creation of two separate commissions representing both sides in the dispute, to holding fresh talks leading to an end to the strike and to loading or unloading the next two vessels which dock at Cosipa's terminal.
They have however rejected a proposal that afterwards, one out of every two boats docked at the terminal should be operated by Cosipa workers and the other by stevedores.
"We will not admit that any other worker do our job," said Ernani Duarte, secretary-general of the National Stevedores' Union.
Stevedores will continue to strike at Santos and will hold a 48-hour national strike from 0700 local Friday unless the issue is resolved, Duarte said.

Cosipa said it had yet to receive official notification that the stevedores have rejected their initial proposal. "We are waiting for this to be formalized to see if negotiations can be resumed," the spokeswoman said.
It was unclear whether a scheduled unofficial meeting between Cosipa chairman Aldo Narcise and union officials had taken place. Neither Cosipa nor unions had any information about the meeting.
